claims.text: Adding a small amount of Hf can improve the high-temperature oxygen resistance of a refractory high-entropy alloy relative to the untreated alloy.
The beneficial effect of Hf alloying should occur above 800 °C.
Hf alloying promotes precipitation of intermetallic compounds such as Ni7Hf2 and Laves phases.
The precipitated intermetallic compounds act as barriers to oxygen diffusion.
Reduced oxygen diffusion decreases oxidation and improves high-temperature oxygen resistance.
Improved oxygen resistance may enhance mechanical properties and durability.
The proposed effect should apply from 800 to 1500 °C in an oxygen-rich environment.
Small Hf additions can improve mechanical properties through Ni7Hf2 and Laves-phase precipitation.

contradictions.description: Mechanical-property enhancement is presented only as a potential secondary outcome, but the falsification rule says that failure to improve mechanical properties alone would falsify the oxygen-resistance hypothesis, even if oxygen resistance improved.
